ety.text: Latin bi-bor. English bi- Proto-Indo-European *kʷel-der. Proto-Indo-European *kʷól-os Proto-Hellenic *pólos Ancient Greek πόλος (pólos)der. Latin polus Proto-Indo-European *h₂el- Proto-Indo-European *-is Proto-Indo-European *h₂élisder.? Proto-Italic *-ālis Latin -ālis Latin -āris Late Latin polārislbor. English polar English bipolar From bi- + polar.

senses.d: Involving or having both extremes or poles at the same time.
ex: And today, the world has become more and more bipolar.

senses.d: Relating to or having bipolar disorder.
ex: If a bipolar person you work with is receiving successful treatment, you might not even know that she is bipolar.

senses.d: Of or relating to an international system in which two states wield most of the cultural, economic, and political influence.

grp.label: relating to or having bipolar disorder
